sn5.4:1.2: Then, in the morning, the bhikkhuni Vijaya dressed …
sn5.4:1.3: she sat down at the foot of a tree for the day’s abiding.
sn5.4:1.4: Then Mara the Evil One, desiring to arouse fear, trepidation, and terror in the bhikkhuni Vijaya, desiring to make her fall away from concentration, approached her and addressed her in verse:
sn5.4:2.2: And I too am a youth in my prime.
sn5.4:2.3: Come, noble lady, let us rejoice
sn5.4:2.4: With the music of a fivefold ensemble.”
sn5.4:3.1: Then it occurred to the bhikkhuni Vijaya:
sn5.4:3.4: This is Mara the Evil One … desiring to make me fall away from concentration.”
sn5.4:3.5: Then the bhikkhuni Vijaya, having understood, “This is Mara the Evil One,” replied to him in verses:
sn5.4:4.3: I offer them right back to you,
sn5.4:4.4: For I, O Mara, do not need them.
sn5.4:5.1: “I am repelled and humiliated By this foul, putrid body,
sn5.4:6.1: “As to those beings who fare amidst form,
sn5.4:6.2: And those who abide in the formless,
sn5.4:6.4: And those peaceful attainments too: Everywhere darkness has been destroyed.”
sn5.4:7.1: Then Mara the Evil One, realizing “The bhikkhuni Vijaya knows me,” sad and disappointed, disappeared right there.
